subtitle: Lesson 8 · T-SQL Foundations

code:
SELECT Name, ListPrice,
  CASE
    WHEN ListPrice = 0 THEN 'Not for Sale'
    WHEN ListPrice < 50 THEN 'Budget'
    WHEN ListPrice < 500 THEN 'Mid-Range'
    ELSE 'Premium'
  END AS PriceTier
FROM Production.Product;
caption: No expression after CASE — each WHEN supplies its own full condition.

code:
-- WRONG ORDER:
CASE
  WHEN ListPrice < 500 THEN 'Mid-Range'
  WHEN ListPrice < 50 THEN 'Budget'
  ELSE 'Premium'
END
caption: A $20 product hits 'Mid-Range' first — 'Budget' never gets a chance.

code:
CASE
  WHEN ListPrice > 1000 AND Color = 'Red'
    THEN 'Premium Red'
  WHEN ListPrice > 1000 THEN 'Premium'
  ELSE 'Standard'
END AS Tier
caption: Each WHEN can combine conditions with AND / OR.
